is turkey part of european plate

No, Turkey is not on the European tectonic plate. [1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Turkey), [2] (https://www.quora.com/Why-is-Turkey-not-considered-a-part-of-Europe-despite-being-geographically-located-in-both-Europe-and-Asia)
Geologically, Turkey sits on the Anatolian tectonic plate (also part of the broader Eurasian plate system and the Alpide belt), while a small southern sliver sits on the Arabian plate. [1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Turkey)
• Tectonic Setting: The Anatolian plate is squeezed and pushed westward and southwestward between the larger Eurasian, African, and Arabian plates. [1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Turkey)
• Geographic vs. Tectonic: While a tiny fraction of Turkey's territory (East Thrace, or about 3% of its landmass) is geographically located in southeastern Europe, the underlying geology and active fault lines (such as the North Anatolian and East Anatolian fault zones) belong to the complex Anatolian/Eurasian collision zone rather than a distinct "European plate". [1] (https://www.britannica.com/place/Turkey), [2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Turkey)
